page: Amazon Web Services p5e.48xlarge is a high-density accelerated computing instance designed for distributed deep learning and large-scale artificial intelligence workloads. It operates on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor and is powered by an AMD x86_64 processor running at 3.6 GHz. The instance provisions 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, coupled with 2048 GB of system memory, providing approximately 10.67 GB of RAM per physical core.

The primary computing capacity is delivered through eight NVIDIA Hopper H200 GPUs providing a combined 1128 GB of high-bandwidth GPU memory. Complementing the GPU array, the instance includes 30400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage for high-throughput dataset caching, along with a 3200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface to facilitate high-speed inter-node communication across large distributed clusters.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the consolidation of eight enterprise-grade accelerators, massive local NVMe capacity, and extreme network throughput reduces cluster node footprint and inter-node communication overhead. The platform is engineered primarily for training large language models, running high-throughput generative AI inference, and executing data-intensive deep learning pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services p5e.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for large-scale distributed artificial intelligence and deep learning workloads. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the platform features 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores on a 3.6 GHz AMD x86_64 processor, paired with 2048 GB of system memory. Its computational core consists of eight NVIDIA Hopper H200 GPUs providing 1128 GB of aggregate GPU memory. For data-intensive pipelines, the server incorporates 30400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 3200 Gbps baseline networking interface to minimize communication bottlenecks across distributed clusters. With dense memory allocation and accelerator bandwidth, the instance is targeted at large language model training, large-scale foundation model fine-tuning, and high-throughput parallel inference tasks.
